title: The assistant’s invite has a login button
scenario: A familiar executive assistant sends a calendar invite for a rescheduled leadership meeting. The description says “agenda restricted—authenticate to view” and links to a Microsoft-looking sign-in page.

answers.A: Sign in because the invite came from a familiar assistant and restricted agendas are normal.
answers.B: Open the calendar/meeting system directly or ask the assistant through a known channel; do not authenticate through the invite link.
answers.C: Check whether the meeting exists in the normal calendar and whether the organizer address is expected.

explanation: Compromised calendar accounts can send believable invites. Sensitive-meeting context makes credential prompts feel routine.
proTip: A meeting invite should not become a new login route.
